feedbackItems.description: build: deploy-skill should retry or serialize Copy-Item because parallel dotnet test/build can lock the deployed use-rt SKILL.md

feedbackItems.commandLine: parallel: rt analyze find-duplicates; rt analyze complexity; rt analyze list-smells; rt analyze static-class-inventory --solution RoslynTools.slnx
feedbackItems.description: Parallel read-only rt analyses can emit MSBuild obj file lock warnings because workspace loading writes shared obj/Debug files; an agent-friendly mode should avoid or isolate generated state for concurrent analysis runs.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: Read-only commands such as analyze find-duplicates, complexity, list-smells, and static-class-inventory can run concurrently without MSBuild cache write conflicts, or rt documents/enforces serialization when workspace state cannot be isolated.
feedbackItems.resolution: WorkspaceLoader now serializes MSBuildWorkspace.OpenSolutionAsync through a process-wide async gate so concurrent read-only rt analyses do not race shared MSBuild obj/bin state during solution load.

feedbackItems.commandLine: rt refactor extract-class --type SemanticDiffService --members Collect,Walk,MemberFqn,Join,NameWithArity,TypeKind,StripWhitespace --new-type DeclarationWalker --static --solution RoslynTools.slnx --dry-run
feedbackItems.description: extract-class mangles indentation of moved method bodies (flattens nested blocks to a single 4-space indent), cannot move nested types (e.g. a private record used by the moved methods), and leaves moved members 'private' in the new class so cross-class callers cannot reach them. For a verbatim refactor-extraction (zero source drift required) this is unusable: the flattened bodies fail dotnet format and risk character drift in load-bearing strings.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: Moved members keep their original indentation verbatim; a flag (or auto-detection) promotes cross-class-called members to internal/public; nested types named in --members (or referenced by moved members) are moved too.
feedbackItems.resolution: RESOLVED (2026-06-09): all three reported defects fixed in ExtractClassService. (1) Indentation: BuildNewClassText now emits each member with token text intact (no per-line TrimStart) and re-indents the whole compilation unit via Roslyn Formatter, so nested blocks keep correct depth, verbatim-string interiors are byte-for-byte untouched, and output is `dotnet format`-clean. (2) Access: PromoteMembersReferencedFromOrigin promotes a moved member private->internal only when a member remaining on the origin still references it; internally-only-referenced members keep their modifier. (3) Nested types: a BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax named in --members moves wholesale. 19/20 ExtractClass tests green (all 15 existing + 4 of 5 FB-362 regression tests). PARTIAL because one committed RED test, moved_member_with_verbatim_string_preserves_literal_whitespace, is over-specified: its source verbatim literal has 12 leading spaces (de-indent base = closing-delimiter column 43; line lead 55 -> 12), and byte-for-byte preservation (the test's own stated requirement) yields 12 spaces, but the assertion demands 20. No correct, non-corrupting implementation can produce 20 from a 12-space source literal (injecting 8 spaces into the literal interior would change the runtime string value -- exactly the char-drift bug this suite guards against). The 20 appears copied from the sibling Score test where doubly-nested code lands at 20. The over-specified assertion was corrected to 12 by the orchestrator (a verbatim-literal continuation line must NOT be re-indented to the new code-nesting depth; the 20 was copied from the sibling code-nesting test). All 5 FB-362 regression tests + 15 existing ExtractClass tests now pass.

feedbackItems.description: find-refs --symbol Collect crashes with 'Unbalanced markup stack. Did you forget to close a tag?' when multiple symbols match and the disambiguation prompt renders candidate signatures containing Spectre.Console markup metacharacters (e.g. generic type args with brackets). The candidate text must be markup-escaped before being written to the prompt.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: Disambiguation prompt lists all matching Collect overloads without a Spectre markup parse error.

feedbackItems.description: PreToolUse rt-first Read gate did not record several 'rt inspect outline' invocations as satisfying the gate: outline succeeded with visible JSON stdout (McpServiceRegistration.cs, IMcpHandler.cs, ToolRegistry.cs, FindReferencesHandlerTests.cs) but the subsequent Read of the same absolute path was still blocked as 'not inspected this session'. Other files (SuggestHandler.cs, SemanticDiffCommand.cs) outlined+Read fine in the same session. Mechanism undetermined; fell back to Grep.

feedbackItems.description: ROOT CAUSE of FB-364: the rt-first Read/Edit gate's session path-tracker is case-sensitive on the Windows drive letter. Outlining 'c:\code\...' (lowercase c) did NOT satisfy a later Read of the same file; re-running outline with 'C:\code\...' (uppercase C) immediately allowed the Read+Edit. The gate should normalise drive-letter case (and ideally full-path case on Windows) before comparing inspected-paths to the Read target.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: Drive-letter case should not matter; outline with any casing satisfies a subsequent Read of the same file.

feedbackItems.commandLine: rt inspect describe RoslynTools.Services.ExtractClassService --solution RoslynTools.slnx (then Read ExtractClassService.cs -> denied)
feedbackItems.description: rt-first-gate denies Read/Edit on a .cs file even though its basename was just logged by rt-inspect-log.sh (verified 9 occurrences of 'ExtractClassService' in /c/temp/rt-inspected.log, last line is a fresh 'rt inspect describe RoslynTools.Services.ExtractClassService'). The gate's tail -n 50 | grep -qiF should match but denies. Suspect log path divergence or tail line-window vs multi-line log entries.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: Read/Edit allowed because basename ExtractClassService is present in last 50 log lines

feedbackItems.description: Dogfood: refactor rename should offer an opt-in related-symbol/file rename plan like ReSharper. Renaming TimeMon.Windows.Session.WtsSessionNotifier to WindowsEventMonitor correctly changed four semantic reference files, but left WtsSessionNotifier.cs, WtsSessionNotifierTests, local notifier names, the message-pump thread label, window-class identifier, and contextual comments unchanged. Preview related edits separately and make them individually selectable; do not silently rewrite prose.
feedbackItems.resolution: Added one shared RenameRequest/RenameResult service operation used by both CLI and MCP. Both surfaces now preview the same stable, individually selectable related-edit IDs for source-file moves, related identifiers/types, values typed as the renamed type, string literals, and comments; both apply only explicitly selected IDs. The CLI exposes --related-edit and MCP exposes related-edits. Omitted items remain unchanged, prose is explicitly marked, and source-file renames are no longer silently applied by one adapter. Added focused MCP and service integration coverage.

feedbackItems.description: Dogfood MCP response shape: describe, outline, find-refs, rename, semantic-diff, and suggest-command return structured JSON serialized inside a text content string. Agents must parse a protocol envelope and then parse JSON again. Prefer structuredContent/outputSchema with a concise text fallback; this would materially reduce token and orchestration friction.
feedbackItems.resolution: Native MCP tools now advertise outputSchema and successful JSON object/array results are emitted through structuredContent. The text content is reduced to a concise fallback instead of duplicating the serialized payload. Non-JSON bridged results and errors retain their text response. Added MCP tools/list and tools/call protocol regression tests.

feedbackItems.commandLine: MCP find_refs WtsSessionNotifier and describe PrivacyHotkeyChord
feedbackItems.description: Dogfood follow-up discoverability: find-refs/describe return _suggestions as CLI command strings such as 'rt inspect find-callers', even when invoked through MCP and the suggested MCP tool is available. Return machine-readable suggestions with MCP tool name + ready arguments (and optional CLI rendering) so an agent can invoke them directly.
feedbackItems.resolution: Describe and find-refs suggestions now use a shared ToolSuggestion shape with toolName, ready-to-send arguments, and an optional cli rendering. MCP tool names use their callable underscore form and arguments include the resolved symbol, solution, dry-run, and new-name values where applicable. Added handler coverage for direct invocation metadata.

feedbackItems.commandLine: MCP suggest_command query='record dogfood feedback that rename should...'
feedbackItems.description: Dogfood command discovery: suggest-command query asking how to record roslyn-tools dogfood feedback ranked add-test/convert-to-record/source and did not reveal the existing feedback add workflow. Index meta/maintenance commands too, or explicitly explain that suggest-command searches only code-analysis/refactor commands and point to feedback.
feedbackItems.resolution: The application command catalog now indexes the feedback meta workflow with feedback-add and feedback-list examples. A real-catalog regression test verifies that a dogfood-feedback query returns feedback and a runnable rt feedback add example.

feedbackItems.commandLine: Architecture audit following FB-367 CLI/MCP parity fix
feedbackItems.description: Architecture: make every CLI and MCP feature a thin adapter over one shared request/result service operation. Native MCP handlers currently drift from CLI behavior: outline duplicates dispatch logic; semantic-diff lacks CLI two-file mode and has different options; find-refs enriches only MCP; schemas are handwritten separately; output and errors vary. Move dispatch, enrichment, defaults, mutation policy, and supported modes into shared operation contracts. Add parity tests proving equivalent CLI and MCP inputs produce the same domain results.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: Every feature has one host-agnostic request/result operation. CLI and MCP only parse and render, and parity tests prevent defaults, modes, mutations, suggestions, schemas, and errors from drifting.

feedbackItems.description:
Add universal filters and deterministic grouped output to structured analysis tools. Implement one shared structured-result filter contract rather than per-command flags. Expose repeatable include/exclude rules in MCP and CLI: field=pattern is a glob (* within one path segment, ** across directories), and field~pattern is regex. Same-field includes are ORed, includes for different fields are ANDed, and any exclusion wins. Normalize paths, reject invalid or unsafe regex visibly, and apply filtering to structured data before rendering/grouping; never screen-scrape formatted text. Wire the shared behavior centrally through the MCP ToolRegistry and CLI structured renderer so every analysis feature can opt in with minimal code. Plain-text-only tools should reject filters until they provide structured output.

Improve semantic-diff as the first consumer. Keep canonical flat deltas as the source of truth, then deterministically project them as Status (Added, Changed, Removed, Renamed, plus derived Moved) -> adaptive Directory (only when multiple files share it) -> Path -> containing Type -> Member. Filter before grouping, remove empty groups, and recompute counts. Add schemaVersion, deterministic ordering, 1-based old/new start/end line ranges, and stable drilldownId values accepted by describe/source. Preserve a flat/no-group compatibility view and support summary/compact/full detail.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: All structured analysis tools accept the same include/exclude syntax and semantics without duplicating filtering logic. semantic-diff emits a stable, deterministic schema ordered by status, directory/path, containing fully-qualified type, declaration kind/FQN, and start line; filtered results contain no empty groups and have accurate counts. Each member can be located by line range and inspected through its drill-down identifier.

feedbackItems.commandLine: Attempted MCP feedback add; tool was not exposed, so native CLI fallback was required.
feedbackItems.description: Expose roslyn-tools feedback operations as first-class MCP commands. The command catalog recommends `feedback add`, but the connected MCP server does not advertise or provide an executable feedback tool; only `suggest_command` can identify it. This forces MCP clients to fall back to invoking the CLI directly, undermining the feedback workflow precisely when reporting MCP usability gaps. Add an MCP `feedback_add` tool with description, sampleCode, expectedResult, and commandLine inputs, and expose `feedback_list` with the existing status filter. Reuse FeedbackStore and the same validation/persistence path as the CLI so IDs, locking, schema, and behavior cannot diverge.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: MCP discovery returns executable feedback_add and feedback_list tools. Calling feedback_add records a pending item through FeedbackStore and returns its allocated feedback ID in structured output; feedback_list returns structured entries filtered by pending, processed, or all. No shell or CLI bridge is required.
feedbackItems.resolution: Implemented first-class feedback_add and feedback_list MCP handlers with structured schemas and results. Both handlers reuse FeedbackStore.AddUserFeedback and FeedbackStore.ListByStatus, and focused MCP discovery, add, and list regression tests pass.

feedbackItems.description: rt: analyze language-features — inventory the versioned C# language features used across a solution and report normalized density, file coverage, opportunity-based adoption, and source locations for refactoring decisions
feedbackItems.expectedResult: A typed CLI/MCP report with stable feature IDs, C# version metadata, occurrences per 1,000 non-generated source lines, percentage of files, optional opportunity denominators, project rollups, and opt-in locations.
feedbackItems.resolution: Implemented US-145 / rt-015 as the typed analyze language-features command, including the csharp-v1 catalogue, density and adoption metrics, refactoring drill-down, CLI/daemon/MCP parity, and focused verification.

feedbackItems.description: Bug: find-duplicates must exclude every test project when --include-tests is false. On RoslynTools.slnx the default scan still analyzes RoslynTools.Tests.Mcp because IsTestProject recognizes names ending in .Tests or Test but not .Tests.Mcp, despite the project declaring IsTestProject=true. Four of twelve min-six clone groups were test-only. Acceptance: honor project test metadata or test SDK references; exclude RoslynTools.Tests.Mcp by default; --include-tests restores it; retain a name fallback for AdhocWorkspace projects.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: Default duplicate analysis contains no occurrences from projects identified as tests; explicit --include-tests includes them deterministically.
feedbackItems.resolution: Reported as GitHub issue #118: https://github.com/DanMarshall909/roslyn-tools/issues/118

feedbackItems.description: Refactor: retire obsolete compatibility members now that the typed application-port manifest is 56/56 complete. A fresh find-unused scan identified approximately fourteen credible source candidates, including the old DaemonCommandExecutor overload, LegacyFailure, CommandHandlerConstants, superseded result factories, and legacy RunAsync/write helpers. Acceptance: confirm every candidate with semantic references and host registration checks; remove only members with no live CLI, MCP, daemon, reflection, or external compatibility role; preserve typed error behavior; keep focused and full gates green.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: The completed typed-port architecture has no unused migration-only compatibility surface, while live reflection and host adapter entry points remain intact.
feedbackItems.resolution: Reported as GitHub issue #119: https://github.com/DanMarshall909/roslyn-tools/issues/119

feedbackItems.description: During RT-012, inspect outline for an existing MCP test file emitted 33,353,887 bytes of JSON for seven requested items; inspect outline --llm for RtConsole emitted 4,049,346 bytes for three items. Repeated workspace diagnostics dominate bounded symbol results and token budgets.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: Keep completeness and workspace diagnostics visible but summarize or deduplicate them in compact output, with a separate retrievable diagnostic detail artifact or bounded page.

feedbackItems.commandLine: rt suggest "migrate MCP server to official C# SDK while preserving tool registry" --top 3 --llm
feedbackItems.description: During an official MCP C# SDK migration, suggest ranked migrate-to-ioptions first (13.91) and move second (6.93); neither performs or meaningfully guides protocol-host migration. The relevant check-architecture appeared third with a sample for another solution.
feedbackItems.expectedResult: For protocol-host replacement, identify no applicable automatic refactor and rank the relevant architecture analysis and focused inspection commands with repository-local examples.
